requirement_text.REQ-151: Builds Letflow's Lua sandbox construction -- the single function every script execution obtains its Lua state from -- and the test suite proving what that state cannot reach. Ports the PROPERTY of R-Co/src/lua/stdlib.zig (143 lines) without porting its mechanism. RESTATEMENT OF LUA-03, AND WHY: R-Co's LUA-03 names a LuaJIT/5.1 module set ("MUST NOT load io, os, package, debug", "MUST load only math, string, table", "MUST remove string.dump, os.execute (if reachable), loadstring, load, loadfile, dofile"). Three reasons that text cannot be adopted verbatim under decision 0014's runtime: (a) loadstring is a Lua 5.1 name absent from 5.3; (b) jit/ffi/bit are LuaJIT-specific and do not exist in Lua 5.3 at all, so R-Co's exclusion of them (including ffi, called 'a COMPLETE sandbox escape') is vacuous here, not satisfied; (c) R-Co's SBX-1 invariant ('prune strictly AFTER open') does not transfer as a mechanism because Lua.new/1 sandboxes by construction, not post-hoc pruning -- there is no open-then-prune ordering to get wrong, but the PROPERTY SBX-1 protects (no window in which a dangerous global is reachable) still must be asserted by test. RESTATEMENT OF LUA-04, AND WHY: LUA-04 ('the sandbox MUST refuse to load Lua bytecode; only source text MAY be loaded') is satisfied STRUCTURALLY -- the adopted runtime parses only Lua source text and has no bytecode loader to disable, so there is no rejection path to test. What IS testable is the absence of every loader: load, loadfile, dofile, and string.dump. THE :sandboxed TRAP: per Lua.new/1's documentation, the :sandboxed option REPLACES the default 27-path deny list rather than adding to it; :exclude is the subtractive option. A naive hardening such as sandboxed: [[:os, :time]] would SILENTLY UN-DENY all 27 defaults including os.execute and load -- this exact trap was caught by REVIEWER during decision 0014's gating. Any custom list this requirement passes MUST restate the full deny-set, and tests MUST assert the DEFAULT denials still hold afterward. SCOPE: (1) a single sandbox-construction function (e.g. Letflow.Engine.Lua.Sandbox.new/0,1) that every script execution uses -- no caller anywhere constructs a Lua state by calling the library directly; (2) enumerate the denied surface against Lua 5.3's ACTUAL stdlib, written out explicitly in source with a per-entry reason comment, in the spirit of R-Co's PRUNED_GLOBALS array; (3) decide coroutine EXPLICITLY, recording the decision and reason in the moduledoc either way; (4) record in the moduledoc that jit/ffi/bit do not exist in Lua 5.3. NOT IN THIS REQUIREMENT: the os-surface time denials (os.time, os.date, os.clock, os.difftime) are REQ-152's (LUA-14). No resource limits, no host API, no executor. GATE: SECURITY-REVIEWER is a hard gate on this requirement -- it is the sandbox boundary itself.

task.description: Write lib/letflow/design/req151-lua-sandbox.md per WF-02_requirement_implementation.md Step 1's procedure: public function signatures, data shapes, invariants, cross-module dependencies, open questions. No implementation code.
acceptance_criteria: a single sandbox-construction function exists (e.g. Letflow.Engine.Lua.Sandbox.new/0,1) and a repo search for the library's own state-construction call across lib/ (restricted to '*.ex' so design docs and this file's own prose are out of scope) shows that function as the only call site, with the real output quoted

a test evaluates each of io.open, io.write, os.execute, os.exit, os.getenv, os.remove, os.rename, os.tmpname, load, loadfile, dofile, require, package, debug, and string.dump from INSIDE a script obtained from that function, and asserts each is nil or raises -- with the real `mix test` output quoted

if any custom :sandboxed list is passed, a test asserts the DEFAULT denials still hold after it (at minimum os.execute and load are still denied from inside a script), explicitly guarding the :sandboxed-replaces-defaults trap; if no custom list is passed here, the moduledoc says so and names REQ-152 as the requirement that adds one

the moduledoc states that this requirement restates LUA-03 rather than satisfying its literal text, and names all three reasons: loadstring is a 5.1 name absent from 5.3; jit/ffi/bit do not exist in Lua 5.3 so R-Co's exclusions of them are vacuous here rather than satisfied; and SBX-1's open-then-prune ordering does not transfer as a mechanism, only as a property

the moduledoc states that this requirement restates LUA-04 rather than satisfying it literally: the runtime has no bytecode loader to disable, so only-source-text holds structurally and there is no rejection path to test -- what is tested instead is the absence of load/loadfile/dofile/string.dump
the deny-set is written out explicitly in source with a per-entry reason, and coroutine's availability is an explicitly recorded decision with a stated reason, not an inherited default
mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass with real output quoted

result.summary: Wrote lib/letflow/design/req151-lua-sandbox.md. Verified Lua.new/1's :sandboxed/:exclude semantics empirically against deps/lua/lib/lua.ex (@default_sandbox is 27 paths, sandboxed: REPLACES it, :exclude subtracts -- confirms the requirement's stated trap). Design fixes the deny-set at 28 entries: the 27 defaults restated explicitly (annotated installed-vs-vacuous per path against deps/lua's actual stdlib, not documentation) plus [:debug], which this design found is installed by tv-labs/lua and NOT in @default_sandbox -- debug.getmetatable/setmetatable bypass __metatable protection and debug.getupvalue/setupvalue read/write closure upvalues, a real non-vacuous gap beyond decision 0014's known gaps. coroutine is explicitly decided: absent from the runtime entirely (no coroutine.ex, not in stdlib.ex's @libraries), so no deny-set entry is added (sandboxing a nonexistent path would fabricate a new global); a test instead asserts coroutine == nil, with a moduledoc note that a future library upgrade adding coroutine must fail that test rather than silently pass unsandboxed. LUA-03 and LUA-04 restatement text specified verbatim for the moduledoc per the requirement's three/one reasons respectively. Test suite spec covers every path AC2 names plus the debug/coroutine findings and a trap-guard regression test for AC3. CRITICAL OPEN QUESTION (OQ-1, design §11): mix.exs on this branch/main currently carries NO {:lua, ...} dependency -- git history shows REQ-148 added it and it was reverted twice (commits 30db07b, 984bbc9) because test/letflow/engine/lua_script_audit_test.exs:419-427 (a REQ-058 'AC5' guardrail) asserts mix.exs has no Lua-shaped dependency 'while the runtime is S5-deferred'. REQ-151 cannot compile without re-adding the dependency, which will re-trigger that exact test failure. This is flagged as blocking and unresolved -- not silently fixed -- since it touches a file outside owned_modules and a locked REQ-058 acceptance criterion; recommended it get explicit REVIEWER attention at Step 2d.
